decisions.heading: We do not give lessons. We give decisions.
decisions.body: Every lesson puts your child inside a choice that has a consequence. They learn because they decided, not because they listened.
decisions.question: You earned 10 coins. What do you do?

decisions.consequenceB: No candy today — but the bike is ten coins closer, and you can feel it.

hero.title: Here, you decide.
hero.subtitle: LittleFounders isn't one more app for your kid. It's an account you open, you link, and you watch over — this is how the Tutor side works.

panel.pendingDetail: Mateo wants to redeem 15 coins for "movie night."
panel.consentOnHint: On — this child's usage data reaches your reports.
panel.consentOffHint: Off — nothing leaves this child's device.

tutor.heading: Everything your child says to the Tutor. You can read it.
tutor.body: Not a summary — the full exchange, turn by turn. And if the Tutor wants to remember something about your child for next time, you approve it first, the old note beside the new one.
tutor.kidLine: "Why does the store want my money so bad?"
tutor.tutorLine: "Great question — stores are built to make you feel like you need things. What made you notice that?"
tutor.memoryPrompt: The Tutor wants to remember this for next time:
tutor.memoryNote: Curious about how ads try to persuade people.
tutor.micNote: Microphone: off by default, on only with your consent.

tasks.heading: Chores with a real reward.
tasks.body: You assign the task and the LF Coins it's worth. You approve it once it's done, and your child decides how to split what they earned. As they show they're ready, you can let small chores count on their own and check them afterwards.
tasks.scenario: You earned 10 LF Coins for finishing your chore. What do you do?
tasks.consequenceSave: 10 coins move into your goal. You're a little closer — and your Tutor can see the progress too.
tasks.consequenceSpend: You ask for something from the catalog your Tutor built, and say why. It waits for their yes, unless it's small enough for the level they gave you.
tasks.consequenceShare: Your Share coins go to a cause or a gift your Tutor picked, and you hear what really happened. Generosity counts here too.

banking.heading: Practice banking, not a bank account.
banking.body: A weekly allowance, a savings bonus you decide to pay, spending limits you set — all of it in LF Coins, all of it reversible, none of it real money.

territory.heading: Their own map, in your view.
territory.body: The same map your child explores — same renderer, nothing redrawn for you. XP, lessons finished, streak, the last time they showed up. Never compared to another child.

privacy.heading: Built private, not patched private.
privacy.body: Usage analytics stay off for each child until you turn them on, one child at a time. The only thing that ever reaches an outside AI model is an age band and a first name. Everything else is checked before it's shown or said out loud.

steps.heading: How to create your Tutor account and link your family
steps.step1Body: Email and password, like any account. A switch already on the form says "I want to be a Tutor" — turning it on sends you straight to verification instead of the usual start.
steps.step2Body: Your name, date of birth, and a photo of your government ID. It's processed to confirm the details and never stored — said before you upload it, not after.
steps.step3Body: A name, a username and a passphrase — chosen by you, not by an email your child doesn't need. Another trusted adult can verify and link to the same child too.
steps.step4Body: Your account and your child's are joined by a verified guardian link. Nothing about theirs is usable without it.

closing.title: Open the account that's actually yours.
closing.body: Free to start. Your child's account comes right after.

hero.title: Frequently asked questions
hero.subtitle: The specific things people ask right before they decide — organized the way a parent actually asks them, not the way the product is built.

whatIs.question: What is LittleFounders?
whatIs.answer: A guided financial-literacy platform where kids and teens learn about money through story-driven decisions and a conversational AI Tutor — not worksheets or lectures.

isFree.question: Is LittleFounders free?
isFree.answer: Yes. Free to start, free to stay — there's no paid tier today, and creating a Tutor account never asks for payment details.

tryWithoutAccount.question: Can my child try it without an account?
tryWithoutAccount.answer: Yes — tap "Start free" and they're straight into a guided lesson, no signup. Progress saves to that browser.

languages.question: What languages does it support?
languages.answer: English, Spanish and Portuguese, switchable anytime from the language picker.

ages.question: What ages is this for?
ages.answer: Roughly 6 to 17. Kids under 13 use a Child account their Tutor creates and supervises; teens 13 and up can also open their own account, though full parental visibility still comes through a linked Tutor.

whatIsTutor.question: What is a "Tutor" account?
whatIsTutor.answer: The adult account — you open it, verify your identity, and every Child account linked to it is yours to see and supervise.

addChild.question: How do I add my child?
addChild.answer: From your Tutor account: a name, a username and a passphrase you choose. No email needed — your child doesn't need one.

twoParents.question: Can both parents supervise the same child?
twoParents.answer: Yes. A second verified Tutor — a co-parent, a grandparent — can link to the same Child account through a single-use invite created from your Tutor panel. The invite works once and expires in 7 days, and you confirm the new Tutor before they can see anything.

howMany.question: How many children can I add?

ownDevice.question: Does my child need their own device?
ownDevice.answer: No — Child accounts work on any shared device; each login is separate from yours.

talksToAI.question: Does my child talk to an AI?
talksToAI.answer: They read and type with a Tutor character who answers in text. Voice is off for minors by default and only turns on with your explicit consent.

privateFromYou.question: Is what my child says to the Tutor private?
privateFromYou.answer: From other users, yes. From you, no — every exchange is visible in your Tutor account, in full, not a summary.

remember.question: Can the Tutor "remember" things about my child?
remember.answer: Only with your approval. It can propose a memory note between sessions; you see the old note beside the new one and approve or decline it.

mentors.question: Who are the mentor characters?
mentors.answer: Four guides — Zara, Rho, Liruf and Dina — each with a distinct personality, leading different lessons.

canBeWrong.question: Can the Tutor be wrong?
canBeWrong.answer: It's an AI model, so yes — it can occasionally explain something imprecisely, the same way any explanation can be phrased better. Everything a Child account sees or hears passes moderation first, and nothing it says replaces your own judgment.

realBank.question: Is this a real bank account?
realBank.answer: No. It's practice, in LF Coins — an educational simulation, never real money.

lfCoins.question: What are LF Coins?
lfCoins.answer: The game's internal currency — earned by finishing tasks and lessons, spent practicing saving, spending and sharing. They have no value outside the platform.

chores.question: How do chores and rewards work?
chores.answer: You assign a task and the LF Coins it's worth: a family contribution or a paid bonus task. Your child splits what they earn into save, spend and share. Every child starts with you approving each chore and reward; as they show they're ready, you can let small ones through on their own, within limits you set.

realMoney.question: Can my child spend real money?
realMoney.answer: No, anywhere in the product. LittleFounders never asks a child for payment details or moves real money.

dataCollected.question: What data do you collect about my child?
dataCollected.answer: The minimum needed to run the product — for a Child account, that's a nickname and an age band. No full name, address or contact info.

moderation.question: Is everything the Tutor says checked first?
moderation.answer: Yes — AI output for a Child account passes moderation before it's shown or spoken.

retention.question: How long do you keep AI Tutor conversations?
retention.answer: Up to 90 days, on a fixed automatic schedule.

noMessaging.question: Can my child message other people?
noMessaging.answer: No. There's no chat, messaging or comments between people, and anything like it would stay off for children unless their Tutor turns it on.

socialRetention.question: How long do you keep who follows whom?
socialRetention.answer: Follows and blocks last until removed or the account is deleted. Unanswered requests expire after 30 days, and closed ones go 30 days later.

analyticsToggle.question: Can I turn off usage analytics for my child?
analyticsToggle.answer: Yes, per child, from your Tutor account — off by default until you turn it on.

coppa.question: Are you COPPA / children's-privacy compliant?
coppa.answer: Our Privacy Notice is built around COPPA and LGPD data-minimization and parental-consent standards — the full legal detail lives there, not summarized here.

contact.question: How do I contact support?
contact.answer: informame@littlefounders.ai, or report a profile from inside the app (Report sits beside Block on any profile).

deleteAccount.question: Can I delete our account?
deleteAccount.answer: Yes, in Settings: it's deleted 14 days later unless you sign in and keep it. Guest accounts go at once; a Tutor deletes a child's.

cancelTutor.question: What happens to my child's account if I cancel mine?
cancelTutor.answer: It's suspended immediately — unusable until an active Tutor account supervises it again. If nothing reactivates it within 90 days, it's deleted.

notTaught.question: Does it teach credit, debt or investing?
notTaught.answer: No. The practice covers earning coins, splitting them into save, spend and share, saving toward goals and asking for rewards. It does not teach borrowing, credit cards, debt, real compound interest, risk, investing or insurance, and the weekly savings bonus is not interest. These are hard to teach well, so we leave them out.

familyRecords.question: How long do you keep chores, rewards and decisions?
familyRecords.answer: Chore photos for 30 days after you decide, and chores, rewards, decisions and notes for 400 days. Coins, goals and rules stay while the account exists. Deleting your child's account deletes all of it.

closing.title: Still have a question?
closing.body: Write to us — a real person reads every message.

curiosity.title: We never open with the lesson
curiosity.body: A character asks the question first. A financial concept nobody asked about is one a kid forgets by dinner, so curiosity always comes before the concept.

needs.title: Feeling first, definition never
needs.body: We do not define what a need is. We put a kid inside a moment where they must decide what matters right now, and the definition arrives after the decision.

goal.title: A goal only counts if it can be pictured
goal.body: We reject abstract targets like save money. Every goal in this curriculum is something a kid can point to and name specifically.

value.title: Worth is felt, not calculated
value.body: Before we ask a kid to compare price and quality, we make them feel the tradeoff, because a formula nobody has felt is one they forget.

question.title: A sharper question beats a right answer
question.body: We value a kid's ability to ask a better question more than their first guess, because that skill outlasts any single lesson.

choice.title: No lesson without a decision
choice.body: If an idea cannot be taught through something a kid chooses live, with a visible consequence, we do not teach it that way. That is the line.

needsVsWants.title: Consequences, not categories
needsVsWants.body: We do not ask a kid to sort a list into need or want. We hand them a limited budget and let the wrong choice run out, live, in front of them.

price.title: A number alone means nothing
price.body: We never show a price without a reason behind it. A number with nothing at stake is trivia, and trivia does not change behavior.

compare.title: Side by side, never in isolation
compare.body: We never ask a kid to judge one option on its own. Comparison only works when the alternative is right there to see.

budget.title: A limit is a plan, not a punishment
budget.body: Where most treat a budget as a restriction, we treat it as the first real plan a kid ever gets to write themselves.

saving.title: The why always comes before the how much
saving.body: We refuse to teach saving as a number in a jar. Every saving goal here is tied, first, to something a kid actually wants.

plan.title: Small steps or it does not ship
plan.body: A goal that cannot be broken into a step small enough for this kid to attempt today is not a lesson we consider finished.

prioritize.title: Order is the lesson, not the list
prioritize.body: We do not teach a kid what to prioritize. We teach them to notice that choosing an order at all is itself the skill.

tradeoff.title: Every yes is also a no
tradeoff.body: We build every choice so picking one option visibly removes another, because a tradeoff a kid only hears about is one they do not believe.

time.title: Patience is designed in, not preached
time.body: Instead of telling a kid to be patient, we design the pacing itself so that waiting is the version that works better.

create.title: An idea only counts once it is built
create.body: We do not reward the idea. We reward the version of it a kid actually finished, however small.

resource.title: Start from what exists, not what is missing
resource.body: Before we ask what a project needs, we make a kid name what they already have. Scarcity thinking starts backwards.

offer.title: A pitch has to survive a real reaction
offer.body: We never grade a kid's idea. We let a character respond to it honestly, the way a real customer would.

cost.title: If the kid did not choose it, it is not cost yet
cost.body: We never hand a kid a materials list. Every cost in this curriculum is the sum of choices the kid made themselves.

revenue.title: Money in has to trace back to a decision
revenue.body: We refuse to teach revenue as a formula. Every sale here connects visibly to an earlier choice, so cause always comes before effect.

share.title: Growth is the metric, not the score
share.body: We measure what a kid is learning to do next, not what they got right today. A percentage tells a family nothing useful.

iterate.title: Wrong is a step, not a stop
iterate.body: A second attempt is not a consolation prize here. It is the expected shape of learning, built into every exercise from the start.

reflect.title: We ask what changed, not what happened
reflect.body: Instead of summarizing a lesson, we ask a kid what they would do differently next time. That question is the actual lesson.

confidence.title: We name the skill, not the win
confidence.body: We never say good job. We say, specifically, what a kid can now do that they could not do yesterday.

nextStep.title: One door, not a hallway
nextStep.body: We never hand a kid a menu of options. There is exactly one next step, chosen for exactly where they are, every time.

question.label: Start with curiosity
question.title: We refuse to open with a fact
question.body: Every adventure starts inside a situation a kid already recognizes, never a definition on a slide.
question.pedagogyTitle: A guess counts more than a right answer
question.pedagogyBody: We let a kid answer wrong first. Correcting a real guess teaches more than confirming a fact they were only told.

practice.label: Learn by doing
practice.title: An idea only counts once it is tried
practice.body: We never explain a concept before a kid has already acted on it, wrong or right.
practice.pedagogyTitle: The mistake is not cleaned up, it is kept
practice.pedagogyBody: We do not erase a wrong choice. We let a kid see exactly what it caused, then hand them a second try.

connection.label: Connect ideas
connection.title: No idea stands alone here
connection.body: We refuse to teach a concept in isolation. Every topic reaches back to one a kid has already mastered.
connection.pedagogyTitle: New knowledge has to attach to something
connection.pedagogyBody: We build every topic as a link, not a chapter, because a fact with nothing to hold onto is one that gets forgotten by Tuesday.

progress.label: Keep moving
progress.title: A win is only useful if it points somewhere
progress.body: We never let progress dead-end. Every completed challenge opens exactly one next one, sized for the kid who just finished it.
progress.pedagogyTitle: Confidence has to be spent immediately
progress.pedagogyBody: We do not let a win sit still. It gets handed a new, reachable challenge before the feeling fades.
